thread:
Maria: Heads-up — scheduling a short, preemptive maintenance window to run a routing reconciliation + pager test for non-prod clusters tomorrow 02:00-02:30 UTC. No planned customer-facing downtime but we'll run traffic cutover drills and a pager test. Keeping it low risk: only staging/dogfood and canary pools. :calendar:

Incident Bot: Reminder: automated pager test will run at 02:05 UTC. On-call recipients: @Ashok, @Kevin P. Reply with "ack" to confirm.

Ashok: Acked. I'll be on the page. Quick q: do we need a statuspage entry for the test, or just internal note?

Maria: We'll post a brief "maintenance (testing)" entry on the status page to avoid surprise alerts from customers who watch it. Short note, no impact. Also sending an internal customer-comms snippet to support just in case.

Jane S: Drafting a short customer message now — will paste below for review.

Jane S: (customer-facing snippet)

```
Planned maintenance (testing): 02:00–02:30 UTC — infrastructure reconciliation and routing test in non-production environments. No user-visible impact expected. We are running routine checks to ensure fast failover and routing health. If you observe any unexpected behavior, please contact support@redwood.ai or check https://status.redwood.ai for updates.
```

Maria: Looks good. Add this to statuspage with component tag "Routing (Non-Prod)" and mark as "maintenance — no impact". Also copy into the support Slack channel so CS has the message.

Kevin P: On the ops side, runbook notes:
1) Pre-check: ensure canary pool has recent model cache snapshot (run `scripts/cache-snapshot.sh canary`).
2) Reconciliation command: `infractl route reconcile --target canary --dry-run` then `--apply` after green checks.
3) Pager test: incident-bot will send a test alert that resolves automatically; if it doesn't, manual failover test: `infractl route failover --simulate`.

Ashok: For handoff — I'm oncall until 02:15 UTC, Kevin will take over for the remainder. I'll paste the handoff note here: "Ashok handing off at 02:15 UTC to Kevin P. If you receive an unexpected pager, triage steps are in the runbook: check canary metrics, confirm KV cache status, and roll back last reconcile via `infractl route rollback`."

Maria: Thanks. A few internal comms items:
- Post to #support with the customer snippet 30 minutes before start.
- Create a statuspage scheduled maintenance with start/end times and link to this thread.
- Ops will run reconciliation in dry-run first; only apply if metrics stable for 5 min.

Incident Bot: Pager test dispatched at 02:05 UTC (test). Target: Ashok.

Ashok: Received test alert, resolved automatically. Confirming metrics look nominal: 99.9th latency unchanged, error rate 0.0% for canary pools. :white_check_mark:

Maria: Great. Kevin, please apply the reconcile at 02:10 UTC and monitor. Post any deviations here.

Kevin P: Applied reconcile `--apply` at 02:11 UTC. Ran smoke checks: token throughput steady, no evidence of cross-pool leakage. Ran a small loadbench against canary with `tools/loadbench -c 50` — no errors.

Jane S: Posted customer snippet to #support and created statuspage scheduled maintenance (internal ID: MP-1976). Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/MP-1976 (internal).

Maria: Thanks everyone. Handoff complete: Ashok -> Kevin at 02:15 UTC.

Incident Bot: Scheduled maintenance MP-1976 started at 02:00 UTC.

Kevin P: I'll keep monitoring until 02:30 UTC. Quick note for post-mortem: log the reconcile duration and whether any route diffs were applied. Use `infractl route diff --since 02:00` to capture.

Maria: Copy — we'll archive the logs and attach to the maintenance ticket. After 02:30, if all good, close the statuspage item and post a completion note here for records.

Incident Bot: Scheduled maintenance MP-1976 ended at 02:30 UTC.

Kevin P: Closing notes: Reconcile applied, diff shows 3 minor route TTL changes (all in canary). No customer impact. Ran post-checks, everything green.

Maria: Closing the statuspage entry and sending final customer update:

```
Maintenance complete: The routing reconciliation and tests in non-production environments completed as scheduled. No customer-visible impact was observed. Thank you for your patience.
```

Jane S: Posted completion to #support and updated MP-1976 on status.

Ashok: Thanks team. Suggestion for next run: include a short internal checklist item to ensure KV cache snapshot success is explicitly logged to ticket (makes audits easier).

Maria: Good suggestion — will add to runbook. Thread archived.
